GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs delivered a strong Q1 2026 with second-highest net revenues ($17.23B) and EPS ($17.55) in history, up 14.4% and 24.3% YoY respectively. ROE of 19.8% and ROTE of 21.3% significantly exceed long-term targets. The firm's #1 global M&A advisory position (32% market share) and record equities revenues ($5.3B) demonstrate durable competitive advantages. However, the stock trades at a P/E of 15.8x, near the upper end of its 12.3-18.4x 12-month range, and P/B of 2.32x is at the top of its 1.5-2.5x range, suggesting the strong Q1 results are largely priced in. Operating cash flow was negative $31.87B in Q1, reflecting the volatile nature of GS's balance sheet-intensive business. The macro backdrop is mixed: rising 10-year yields (4.41%) and elevated oil prices ($98/bbl) create headwinds, while the Basel III capital requirement reduction of 2.4% for Category I banks is a tailwind for capital returns. Near-term catalysts are limited post-Q1 earnings, with the next major event being Q2 results in late July. The score reflects solid fundamentals and trajectory offset by full valuation.
